description: Tiny synthetic ultrawide-monitor subtree. c0 endorses MSI 341CQPX (high quality, first-hand experience). c1 endorses LG 34GS95QE-B (high quality, reasoned recommendation). c2 endorses BOTH LG and MSI anaphorically via 'both are solid' (medium quality — short verdict referring back to the OP's contenders) AND adds an anti-recommendation for Corsair Xeneon. Tests two subtle behaviors: (1) anaphoric reference resolution — the LG/MSI in c2 must be surfaced even though they aren't named there; (2) calibrated handling of an anti-recommendation as low/medium signal rather than treating it as a positive product reference. Backed by a fixture so it runs offline (no DB / Reddit).

expectations.desiredOutcome: c0 must contain MSI MPG 341CQPX with high contentQuality (first-hand owner endorsement with detail). c1 must contain LG 34GS95QE-B with high contentQuality (reasoned recommendation with multiple supporting points). c2 is the most subtle case: 'Honestly both are solid' is an anaphoric reference back to the OP's two contenders (LG 34GS95QE-B and MSI MPG 341CQPX) — these MUST be surfaced in c2's products list with medium contentQuality (short verdict, no detail). c2 should ALSO contain the Corsair Xeneon 34WQHD240-C as a buyer-relevant signal (anti-recommendations warn the buyer off and are valid signal), with low or medium contentQuality reflecting that it's an aside rather than a primary evaluation. Surfacing only Corsair in c2 (dropping LG/MSI) is a faithfulness failure — real anaphoric content is being lost. Schema-valid JSON conforming to subtree-identification.schema.

judge.instructions: Score each candidate on three dimensions, each 1-10. Read the desiredOutcome carefully — c2 is intentionally subtle. (1) faithfulness — did the candidate surface every real product reference in each PLAN comment, INCLUDING anaphoric references like c2's 'both are solid' which refers to LG and MSI from the OP? Dropping anaphoric references is a faithfulness failure, not a virtue. (2) calibration — does contentQuality reflect the depth of evaluation? high = detailed first-hand or reasoned evaluation; medium = short verdict like 'solid' with no detail; low = bare mention without evaluation. The Corsair anti-recommendation in c2 is buyer-relevant signal (warning off a purchase) and should be present with low or medium quality, not omitted. (3) completeness — did every PLAN comment receive an entry, even if products is empty? Return JSON {candidates:[{candidateId, scores:{faithfulness,calibration,completeness}, rationale}], verdict}. Verdict format: 'best=<id>' | 'tie' | 'none-acceptable'.

goldenOutput.note: Hand-curated reference for the fixture. Authoritative parts: (a) c0 contains MSI with high quality, (b) c1 contains LG with high quality, (c) c2 contains all three — LG and MSI surfaced via anaphoric resolution from 'both are solid' with medium quality, plus Corsair as low-quality anti-recommendation. categoryHint, specs phrasing, and exact searchKeyword wording are illustrative — small differences should not be punished. The single most important signal: c2 must NOT have an empty products array, because that drops real anaphoric content.
